In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both cool spots and opacity uncertainties are likely to be present in the primary.
2M0535–0545 is likely a young, spotted, and very low-mass binary, and that there are likely opacity errors in the TiO- molecular bands of PHOENIX.
the TiO- and K I fits are in good agreement, but the TiO- fits are more robust because of their higher sensitivity to T eff.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have obtained a spectrum of a very young substellar object that is free of significant contamination from the other component in the binary.

the present analysis, while not conclusive on the nature of the photospheric spots on 2MASS0535, has nevertheless provided the first quantitative test of model opacity predictions at substellar gravities.
, while the primary is likely spotted, the nature of the spots is still uncertain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T eff reversal between 2MASS primary and secondary can be understood in terms of a cool spot distribution that is not symmetric between the two components.
the TiO- and K I bands are both sensitive to the surface gravity, and that the K I band can be used to determine the surface gravity of a brown dwarf, even when the TiO- is not observable.
the TiO- and K I bands are not necessarily good tracers of the primary's true T eff, and that the T eff reversal between components may be explained by cool spots rather than a higher-mass primary.
